mechanism_narrative: A higher level of CPIAUCSL (current index value) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as elevated inflation expectations compress equity risk premiums and increase discount rates.
failure_condition: The correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is not negative (i.e., correlation >= 0) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an ultra-loose monetary policy that reduces risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS (below 0.5%) and 20-day returns is not positive (i.e., correlation <= 0) over a 3-year rolling window, or the signal fails to predict positive returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 5% combined with a federal funds rate below 1% indicates a recessionary economy with ultra-loose monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to depressed corporate earnings and heightened risk aversion.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (UNRATE>5% AND FEDFUNDS<1%) fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by quarterly GDP growth above 2% annualized and unemployment rate below 4%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to overvaluation and the expectation of monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: The late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1>2% and UNRATE<4%) fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of instances, or the rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals weak labor market conditions that depress consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is not negative (i.e., correlation >= 0) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 8% signals a severe labor market downturn that depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is not negative (i.e., correlation >= 0) over a 3-year rolling window, or the threshold condition (UNRATE>8%) fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) above 650,000 units indicates a strong housing market and robust consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and 20-day returns is not positive (i.e., correlation <= 0) over a 3-year rolling window, or the threshold condition (HOUST>650) fails to predict positive returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS above 360,000 million dollars) combined with robust industrial production (INDPRO above 100) indicate a healthy economy with rising corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (RSAFS>360000 AND INDPRO>100) fails to predict positive returns in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.
